newsitem.title: GABON: Congo mediators seek inter-African force.
newsitem.headline: Congo mediators seek inter-African force.

text.p: Mediators trying to broker peace in the Congo Republic capital Brazzaville will ask the U.N. Security Council to support deployment of an inter-African force in the city, U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said on Thursday.

Sahnoun told a news conference that Gabon's veteran president, Omar Bongo, would put forward the request on behalf of the mediators, who tried but failed to rally the warring parties around a peace plan on Monday.

"The International Mediation Committee on the Crisis in Congo has authorised its president (Bongo) to inform the U.N. Security Council as soon as possible with a view to deploying an inter-African force to help return peace and stability to Congo," Sahnoun said.

Sahnoun, who visited Brazzaville on Wednesday and had talks with the warring parties, said the Organisation of African Unity body for preventing, managing and settling conflict would also be informed so that it could help.

He was speaking after talks with Bongo. Other members of the committee include the president of Mali, Chad and of the Central African Republic, where an African peacekeeping force is in place after similar clashes in late 1996 and early 1997.

Supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and those of his predecessor and rival Denis Sassou Nguesso, Congo's former military leader, have fought fierce ethnic and political battles in Brazzaville since June 5, sowing death and destruction and dividing the city into rival camps.
A 72-hour truce ends of Friday. The two warring parties told Sahnoun on Wednesday they would do their best to extend it.
